name: POST /curation/{source_id}/approve
user_story: As a curator, I want to approve a pending submission (optionally minting a DOI and applying metadata fixes) so that it is published, DOI-registered, indexed, and the submitter is notified.
expected_behavior: Curator-only. Requires status==pending_curation (400 otherwise). Records 'approved' curation_history with curator_id+timestamp. If metadata_updates provided, deep_merges into dataset_mdata. Sets status=approved, approved_at/by, upserts. Then ALWAYS enqueues a publish job (mint_doi flag controls only the DOI step). In inline mode, refreshes record to reflect publish result (status->published, doi). Publish pipeline: _mint_doi_for_submission (DataCite mint/update with version-aware logic), search ingest (build_gmeta_entry), prior-version reindex with latest=false, status=published, approval email, embedding job.

side_effects: DynamoDB upsert (approved), then upsert (published) in publish job | DataCite DOI mint/update (real client if creds set, else Mock) | Globus Search ingest (real or Mock per USE_MOCK_SEARCH) + prior-version reindex | SES approval email to submitter | Embedding job (OpenAI) enqueue

But re-running the publish job (SQS retry, maxReceiveCount=3) re-mints/updates DOI and re-ingests — mint_doi path generates a deterministic suffix so DataCite update path is idempotent; version DOI suffix appends -v<version> each call (idempotent on same version).'}
sync_parity_posture: Search ingest builds the v1-compatible dc/mdf/data GMetaEntry (search_client.build_gmeta_entry) — this is the schema that MUST match the v1 Globus Search index (1a57bbe5...). DOI suffix derived from source_id via _generate_suffix. Critical sync surface.
issues_summary: [high/functionality] _process_publish_submission sets status='published' unconditionally at the end even if DOI minting failed AND/OR search ingest failed (both failures are only logged as warnings). A dataset can be marked 'published' in Dynamo while absent from the search index and/or without a DOI, silently breaking discoverability and the published==indexed contract. ;; [med/functionality] In SQS mode the approve handler returns 200 with status 'approved' (not 'published') and a queued publish_job; the result['doi'] is only populated in inline mode. Clients cannot tell from the response whether publishing/DOI succeeded, and there is no status callback. Combined with the unconditional 'published' flip, partial failures are invisible. ;; [med/sync] build_gmeta_entry derives mdf.source_name as source_id.rsplit('-',1)[0]. For v2 generated source_ids ('mdf-<uuid>') this yields 'mdf', and for collision-suffixed ids it strips the suffix — both diverge from the v1 contract where source_name is a meaningful dataset name. This pollutes the v1-compatible search doc's source_name field used for version grouping/faceting. ;; [med/functionality] metadata_updates deep_merge in approve stores dataset_mdata as a Python dict on the record (submission['dataset_mdata']=existing_metadata), then upsert_submission(Dynamo) stores it as a native Map while put paths elsewhere store it as a JSON string. This dual representation (dict vs JSON string) of dataset_mdata across code paths invites parse inconsistencies (every reader must handle both). ;; [low/functionality] Approve uses datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() WITHOUT the 'Z'/+00:00 normalization used elsewhere (submissions.py uses .replace('+00:00','Z')), producing inconsistent timestamp formats ('+00:00' here vs 'Z' in submit/edit) across the same record's fields.

SQS worker handle_sqs_event processes each record, returning batchItemFailures for partial-batch retries (DLQ after maxReceiveCount=3). EventBridge schedule (rate 6h) triggers cleanup_transfers.

OK."}

name: Identity resolution: dev X-User-Id headers vs production Globus userinfo
user_story: As the platform operator, I want production requests authenticated against Globus and dev-header auth gated to local runtimes, so that nobody can spoof identity in production by sending an X-User-Id header.
expected_behavior: AUTH_MODE=dev only honored when LOCAL_DEV_AUTH or AWS_SAM_LOCAL truthy (get_auth_mode forces 'production' otherwise). In dev mode, identity is taken from X-User-Id / X-User-Email / X-User-Name headers or LOCAL_* env defaults. In production, the Bearer token is validated by calling Globus AuthClient.userinfo() (not introspect), 'sub' becomes user_id; missing 'sub' or AuthAPIError -> 401.
inputs: Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, X-User-Id/X-User-Email/X-User-Name (dev), X-MDF-Token, X-Groups-Token; env AUTH_MODE, LOCAL_DEV_AUTH, AWS_SAM_LOCAL, GLOBUS_CLIENT_ID/SECRET.
outputs: AuthContext{user_id, name, user_email, identities, group_info, dependent_token}.
side_effects: Network calls to Globus Auth userinfo on EVERY request; optional dependent-token exchange (ConfidentialAppAuthClient) and GroupsClient.get_my_groups call.
error_paths: Missing Authorization -> 401 (L52-53); empty bearer -> 401 (L56-57); AuthAPIError -> 401 (L72-73); missing sub -> 401 (L76-77); any other Exception -> 401 with message echoing exception 'Authentication failed: {e}' (L123-124).
security_posture: CONTROL: server-side Globus token validation via userinfo; dev-header bypass guarded by get_auth_mode (L23-25). POSTURE: mostly sound. GAPS: (1) No introspection/userinfo result caching -> every authenticated request makes 1-3 synchronous Globus API calls (DoS / latency amplification, and a Globus outage hard-fails all auth). (2) Group-fetch failures are swallowed (L97-98, L110-111) so group_info silently empties -> a transient Groups API error downgrades a curator/submitter to no-groups, which combined with ALLOW_ALL_CURATORS=true (see SEC-02) is masked but with strict groups would deny legitimate users. (3) Exception detail leaks raw exception text to the client (L124). (4) userinfo() accepts ANY valid Globus token for ANY resource server (comment L62-66 acknowledges this) — there is no audience/scope check, so a token minted for an unrelated Globus app is accepted as a valid MDF identity.
deployability_posture: AUTH_MODE wired from template param (template.yaml:212), forced to dev only for IsDevAuth stacks. Dev/prod parity: dev uses header identity, prod uses Globus. No rollback concern.
sync_parity_posture: n/a
issues_summary: [med/security] Production token validation uses userinfo() which accepts any valid Globus access token regardless of audience/scope; no audience or resource-server check binds the token to the MDF app. ;; [med/security] No caching of userinfo/group lookups: each request triggers synchronous Globus calls; a Globus outage hard-fails all auth and adds latency / cost. ;; [low/security] Exception text echoed to client in 401 detail (information disclosure). ;; [low/functionality] Group-fetch failures are swallowed, silently emptying group_info and thus revoking group-based permissions on transient errors.

name: Curator authorization (is_curator / require_curator) and ALLOW_ALL_CURATORS bypass

error_paths: 403 'You do not have curator permissions'.
security_posture: CONTROL: group-membership-based curator gate. POSTURE: BROKEN in deployed config. ALLOW_ALL_CURATORS=true is set in BOTH staging AND prod samconfig overrides (samconfig.toml:50,64). With that flag, is_curator returns true for ANY authenticated Globus user (L155-156), so any logged-in user can approve/publish datasets, mint REAL production DataCite DOIs (prefix 10.18126), soft-delete any submission, and read cross-org/admin data. The template 'auto' default would set false in prod, but the explicit samconfig override re-enables it.

sync_parity_posture: n/a

name: configure_app_middleware: request-id, body-size cap, in-memory rate limiting, request logging
user_story: As the platform operator, I want per-actor rate limiting, request-size caps, and request IDs so that abusive or oversized requests are bounded and every request is traceable.
expected_behavior: Middleware assigns request_id (from X-Request-Id or uuid4), enforces MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 1MiB) on POST/PUT/PATCH via Content-Length and actual body read, applies per-path per-actor rate limits (submit 20/min, stream-create 30, stream-upload 60, stream-mutation 90, default 120) in a sliding window, returns 413/429 JSON, logs structured JSON per request, and echoes X-Request-Id on responses.
inputs: Request headers (x-request-id, content-length, x-user-id, authorization), env RATE_LIMIT_* / MAX_REQUEST_BYTES / RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS.
outputs: 413/429 JSON responses; X-Request-Id header; structured logs.
side_effects: Mutates module-global _RATE_LIMIT_STATE (in-memory deque per actor key); reads full request body into memory for size check.
error_paths: 413 on oversized body; 429 with Retry-After on rate-limit; re-raises on downstream exception (logged).
security_posture: CONTROL: app-level rate limit + size cap + request id. POSTURE: useful defense-in-depth but FUNDAMENTALLY INEFFECTIVE on Lambda. The rate-limit state is process-memory only; with reserved concurrency 10 (API) each cold/warm container has its own counter and Lambda recycles containers, so effective limits are ~N*configured and reset frequently — not a real global limiter. No security HEADERS are added (no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy) despite the function name 'security_and_logging_middleware'. Actor key falls back to client IP which behind API Gateway/Mangum may be unreliable. The full-body read for size enforcement happens AFTER Content-Length check but still buffers up to the cap.
deployability_posture: Pure code; tunable via env. No IaC drift. Real throttling is delegated to HttpApi DefaultRouteSettings (IAC-04).
sync_parity_posture: n/a
issues_summary: [med/security] No HTTP security headers set (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, Referrer-Policy) despite middleware named 'security_and_logging_middleware'. ;; [low/functionality] Rate limiter uses per-container in-memory state on Lambda; effective limit scales with concurrency and resets on container recycle — not a reliable global limit.
